newsitem.title: UK: UK manufacturing demand sluggish in September - CBI.
newsitem.headline: UK manufacturing demand sluggish in September - CBI.

text.p: British manufacturing demand was little improved in September but demand from overseas picked up a little although it remains at weak levels, the Confederation of British Industry said on Friday.
Manufacturers were more hopeful about the future. With stock levels falling, output is expected to increase while prices hold steady.

The CBI's monthly industrial trends survey found only 17 percent of the 1,217 UK companies surveyed said total orders were above normal while 26 percent said they were below -- a negative balance of nine percent.
This is a slight improvement on August when the balance of firms was minus 10 percent which in turn was distinctly less gloomy than the minus 22 percent reading in the July survey.
"The improvement in demand seen over the past few months is encouraging, although manufacturers continue to be hampered by weak exports," said Sudhir Junankar, CBI associate director of economics.
A negative balance of 11 percent of firms said export demand was worse than normal. But that represents an improvement on August, when the balance was minus 14 percent.

Manufacturers' expectations were more encouraging. A positive balance of 20 percent of firms expected output to increase markedly over the next four months -- a small deterioration in sentiment from August when the balance was 22 percent.
The outlook means few firms expect to be able to pass on higher prices. As many firms expect the trend in prices to be down as up.

"The news on prices is much better as companies expect the unchanged trend in domestic prices to continue in the coming months," Junankar said. "This is promising, as it is likely to exert downward pressure on overall inflation over the short-term."

The overhang in manufacturers' stocks continues to be a problem but is slowly being unwound, the CBI said. A positive balance of 14 percent of firms said stocks were more than adequate, but that reading is the lowest since August 1995.

"With companies starting to make inroads in their stocks of unsold finished goods, the output increases predicted in this survey suggest that manufacturing industry in the UK is poised to recover," Junankar said.
The monthly trends survey canvassed 1,217 manufacturing companies, representing 50 industries and accounting for about half of the UK's manufactured exports and output of some two million employees.
